correctness.rationale: A necessary-and-sufficient local witness characterization proves a bijection between super dominating sets and a subset U of omitted roots with at most one omitted pendant at every vertex in V\N_G[U]. Counting its choices yields the displayed polynomial. Minimum exponent, multiplicity and two-omission coefficient follow by exact extraction; isolated and disconnected cases are covered, with \(r_v\ge1\) essential. Standalone verifier performs 2,435,884 direct-definition checks across 1,150 graph/multiplicity instances, and independently checks component and high-degree formulas. The infinite theorem rests on proof, not finite tests.

originality.rationale: Published full-text comparisons identify the earlier scalar formula for ordinary coronas (Klein et al., Theorem 18), a distinct neighborhood-corona invariant and minimum enumerations (Ghanbari et al.), and a polynomial study of unrelated elementary graph families and universal-vertex addition (Kaidash 2023). None gives the complete heterogeneous leaf-corona counting bijection, component-factorized minima, or edge-reading coefficient. Actual published-record semantic searches identified only different invariants or different graph families. The later Kaidash chapter was unavailable beyond its abstract; its possible implicit content remains an acknowledged nonzero originality risk. Noncoverage of all published or unindexed work is not asserted.
residual_risks: The full 2024 Kaidash chapter could not be inspected and its abstract does not identify which graph families it enumerates; implicit or partial overlap cannot be excluded.
Unindexed or differently termed earlier super-domination enumerators may exist; published result searches do not establish universal priority.

value.rationale: A full cardinality enumerator for a broadly used natural graph operation with arbitrary base graphs and nonuniform private pendants is more informative than existing scalar minima. The explicit \(2^n\)-term expression yields component-factorized counts of minimum placements and an edge-sensitive coefficient that reconstructs base edge counts under homogeneous attachment. These precise quantities describe multiplicities and structural sensitivity at all cardinalities; the contribution is not a restatement of \(\gamma_{sp}=R\), a textbook one-line relabeling, or a finite curiosity.
